hero.lead: A nation of 64.7 million that pioneered a first-of-its-kind wildlife conservation bond, and still makes more than nine-tenths of its electricity from non-renewable sources, most of it coal.

capital.heading: 17 instruments. Debt stabilised, a rhino bond, a transition partnership, and loans for power, freight, water and cities.

record.text: Just Energy Transition Partnership pledges, with the multilateral development banks, December 2025; the initial mobilisation was $8.5 billion
Gross loan debt stabilised at 78.4% of GDP in 2025/26, and Treasury expects the ratio to decline over the rest of the decade
World Bank Infrastructure Modernization and Job Creation Development Policy Loan, signed July 2026
World Bank Metro Trading Services Program, the first Program-for-Results in South Africa, for about 22 million people
Wildlife Conservation Bond: success payment up to $13.76 million, tied to black rhino population growth

register.name: International bonds due 2037 and 2055
register.detail: Announced 5 December 2025 · US$1.75 billion each · re-offer yields 6.25% (2037) and 7.375% (2055)
register.note: Order book of US$13.1 billion, about 3.7 times covered
register.text: Two US dollar bonds of US$1.75 billion each, sold in international capital markets to fund managers, insurers, pension funds and banks from the United Kingdom, North America, Europe, Asia and Africa. Demand reached US$13.1 billion.

register.name: Infrastructure and Development Finance Bond
register.detail: Issued 9 December 2025 · RI2036 (10 years, 8.575%) R6.996 billion and RI2041 (15 years, 9.13%) R4.799 billion · bids above R26 billion
register.note: South Africa’s first bond of its kind
register.text: Proceeds may be used only for projects under the Budget Facility for Infrastructure. It ties borrowing directly to public infrastructure investment.

register.name: Infrastructure Modernization and Job Creation Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Release of 16 July 2026 · IBRD · signed, announced 21 July 2026 · 15 years, 3 years’ grace, six-month SOFR plus 1.35%
register.note: The fourth development policy loan since 2022
register.text: Supports a competitive wholesale electricity market, private investment in transmission, 300,000 new household connections by December 2027, competition among rail operators, the first port terminal concession in Durban and private water service providers. World Bank Group modelling points to almost 600,000 more and better-paid jobs by 2032.

register.name: South Africa Metro Trading Services Program
register.detail: Announced 7 November 2025 · Program-for-Results, the first in South Africa · part of a $3 billion (R55 billion) government effort
register.note: Water, sanitation, electricity and waste in eight metros
register.text: Pays on results for better water, sanitation, electricity and waste services in Buffalo City, Cape Town, Ekurhuleni, Johannesburg, Tshwane, eThekwini, Mangaung and Nelson Mandela Bay, home to about 22 million people.

register.name: Infrastructure Modernization for South Africa Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved, announced 5 June 2025 · signed, announced 23 June 2025 · 16 years, 3 years’ grace, six-month SOFR plus 1.49%
register.note: Energy transmission, freight transport and a low-carbon transition
register.text: Budget support for reforms that draw investment into power transmission, widen grid access, create an independent freight transport regulator and restructure Transnet. It builds on the energy transition loan of 2023.

register.name: Sustainable and Low-Carbon Energy Transition Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved, announced 25 October 2023 · development policy loan
register.text: Supports the unbundling of Eskom, competition in the electricity market, private investment in renewable energy, including by households and small businesses, and stronger carbon pricing.

register.name: Komati Just Energy Transition Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 4 November 2022 · World Bank loan $439.5 million, Canadian concessional loan $47.5 million, ESMAP grant $10 million
register.note: Repurposing a coal plant with 220 MW of renewables and 150 MW of batteries
register.text: Decommissions the Komati coal-fired power plant and repurposes it with solar, wind and battery storage, with a transition plan for workers and business support expected to benefit about 15,000 people in the community.
by: Canadian Clean Energy and Forest Climate Facility

register.name: Wildlife Conservation Bond
register.detail: Priced 23 March 2022 · issued by IBRD · outcome bond, matures 31 March 2027
register.note: Success payment up to $13.76m, tied to black rhino population growth
register.text: A first-of-its-kind, outcome-based bond issued by the World Bank. Investors forgo coupons and, at maturity, receive a success payment of up to US$13.76 million, funded by a grant from the Global Environment Facility, if black rhino numbers grow in Addo Elephant National Park and the Great Fish River Nature Reserve.

register.name: New Development Bank loan for the Metro Trading Services Reform Programme
register.detail: Concluded, announced 15 September 2026 · 16 years, 3 years’ grace, daily SOFR plus 1.18508%
register.note: Performance-based, with the World Bank, AIIB, KfW and AFD
register.text: Finances upgrades to metropolitan water and sanitation, electricity and solid waste services, paid against independently verified targets approved by metro councils.

register.name: New Development Bank loan for the Olifants Management Model Program, Stage 1
register.note: Bulk water from Flag Boshielo Dam
register.text: Funds the public share of a bulk water scheme drawing on the Olifants River, which will supply raw water to industry and potable water to communities in Mogalakwena, Limpopo. It is a public-private partnership with industrial users.

register.name: New Development Bank loans for the Limpopo Central Hospital and the Magalies Bulk Water Supply Scheme
register.detail: Announced 28 August 2026 · 10 years including 4 years’ grace · daily SOFR plus 0.93508%
register.note: US$200 million for the hospital and US$205 million for water
register.text: Builds a 488-bed tertiary hospital in Polokwane, the province’s main referral hospital, and improves the supply of drinking water in Bela-Bela, Modimolle-Mookgophong, Mogalakwena, Moretele, Moses Kotane and Rustenburg.

register.name: Mpumalanga Municipal Utility Reform Programme
register.detail: Approved, release of 16 July 2026 · backed by a UK FCDO guarantee under the Just Energy Transition Partnership
register.note: About 1.2 million people in four municipalities
register.text: Makes electricity and water services more efficient and reliable in eMalahleni, Lekwa, Govan Mbeki and Mbombela, in the coal region at the centre of the energy transition. Disbursements follow verified results.
by: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

register.name: AIIB co-financing of the South Africa Metro Trading Services Program
register.detail: Approved 24 June 2026 · sovereign · World Bank lead co-financier under its Program-for-Results policy
register.note: Water, electricity and waste in the metros
register.text: AIIB’s sovereign loan alongside the World Bank programme for water, sanitation, electricity and waste services in the eight metros.

register.name: Infrastructure Governance and Green Growth Programme
register.detail: Signed, announced 25 July 2025 · third development policy operation · 15 years, 3 years’ grace, daily SOFR plus 1.22%
register.text: Budget support for reforms that make energy and transport infrastructure more efficient, resilient and sustainable. Co-financiers of the operation include the World Bank, KfW, JICA and the OPEC Fund.

register.name: Just Energy Transition Partnership
register.detail: Investment plan published 7 November 2022 · 12-month leaders’ update, 9 December 2025 · the United States withdrew on 28 February 2025
register.note: Pledges with multilateral development banks; the initial mobilisation was $8.5 billion
register.text: Finance from the United Kingdom, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany and the Netherlands, other bilateral partners and multilateral development banks for the shift away from coal. Partner pledges stand at $10 billion, $12.4 billion with other bilateral pledges and $13.7 billion with the multilateral development banks.

register.name: IFC and FirstRand Bank (FNB)
register.detail: Release of 18 September 2025 · loan of about R1.8 billion
register.note: For underserved micro, small and medium enterprises
register.text: A loan that FNB will lend on to underserved small businesses in high-impact sectors that have long struggled to find finance.

register.name: IFC and Balwin Properties
register.detail: Release of 15 April 2025 · local-currency loan, about $58 million
register.note: 16,468 homes at Mooikloof City, east of Pretoria
register.text: Finances homes for lower-to-middle income buyers in EDGE Advanced certified apartments. It adds certified resource-efficient homes for families on modest incomes.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Wildlife
items.label: Wildlife Conservation Bond, March 2022
items.text: Investors receive a success payment at maturity, in 2027, only if the black rhino population grows.
items.alt: A black rhino in the Eastern Cape

items.name: The Sun and Wind
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Among the strongest solar and wind resources anywhere, on a grid still run mostly on coal.
items.alt: Solar and wind farms in the Northern Cape

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.alt: A platinum mine in the Bushveld

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Farms and rangeland across four-fifths of the country.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Nearly two in three live in cities.

items.name: Balwin Properties
items.text: A property developer building homes for lower-to-middle income buyers. With an IFC loan of ZAR 1 billion it is building 16,468 units at Mooikloof City, east of Pretoria.

items.name: Kenhardt solar and battery project (Scatec)
items.text: 540 MW of solar with 225 MW / 1,140 MWh of battery storage, in commercial operation since December 2023. It delivers 150 MW of dispatchable power to Eskom every day from 5 am to 9:30 pm under a 20-year agreement.

items.name: SPARK Schools
items.text: A network of 26 affordable private schools serving more than 17,000 scholars, with monthly fees from about R3,000 for primary school.

items.name: FNB (FirstRand Bank)
items.text: Lends to micro, small and medium enterprises across South Africa, and will on-lend a US$100 million IFC loan to underserved small businesses in high-impact sectors.
